title: Harden the web app with a strict nonce-based CSP and Trusted Types
body:
## Context
The web app targets **OWASP ASVS 5.0 L2** (decision 8) and DOM-XSS is the primary web threat, especially when rendering user note HTML/markdown. The mandated defence is a **strict, nonce-based CSP** (`script-src 'nonce-{random}' 'strict-dynamic'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'none'`) plus **`'wasm-unsafe-eval'`** for the CanvasKit/skwasm/whisper WASM runtime, and **Trusted Types** (`require-trusted-types-for 'script'`) routing every DOM sink through a DOMPurify policy (`docs/platform/web.md` §9, ADR-0010 Security impact, secure-coding-checklist §6.2). Trusted Types is Chromium-only today, so markdown/HTML MUST also be sanitised unconditionally for Safari/Firefox. This is a p0 gate rule.

## Scope
**In:** per-response nonce injection into the served `index.html`; the CSP header/meta with strict-dynamic + wasm-unsafe-eval; a Trusted Types policy + DOMPurify on all note-derived HTML/markdown; removal of any inline-script reliance in the bootstrap.
**Out:** COOP/COEP ({{SN-WEB-015}}), SRI + other headers ({{SN-WEB-016}}), edge/CDN delivery of headers ({{SN-WEB-017}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The served CSP is nonce-based with `'strict-dynamic'`, `object-src 'none'`, `base-uri 'none'`, `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`; no `unsafe-inline`/`unsafe-eval`, no host allow-list as primary defence.
- [ ] `require-trusted-types-for 'script'` is set; every DOM sink write goes through the DOMPurify-backed policy; a violation is reported (report-only rollout first).
- [ ] A note containing `<script>`/`onerror=`/`javascript:` markdown renders inert on Chromium, Safari and Firefox (sanitised unconditionally).
- [ ] ZAP baseline scan shows no CSP/XSS finding for the web app.

## Technical notes
Nonce is generated per request at the origin/edge and stamped into `flutter_bootstrap.js` loader tags; the WASM runtime needs `'wasm-unsafe-eval'`. DOMPurify + a named Trusted Types policy in the web entry (self-hosted, no CDN at runtime). Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §9 and secure-coding-checklist §6.2. Roll out with `Content-Security-Policy-Report-Only` first.

## Security & privacy
Kills DOM-XSS (TM-I-06): MASVS-PLATFORM-2, OWASP-A03, CWE-79, ASVS 5.0 web-frontend chapter. Sanitise regardless of CSP (defence in depth). CSP violation reports must not include note content. No secrets in headers.

## UX notes
No visible UI, but any markdown/HTML in notes (quote/callout/code blocks, PRD-ED-179/180/181) must still render correctly across all 17 looks + dark after sanitisation — verify no legitimate formatting is stripped. A11y unaffected.

## Test plan
`app/test/web/csp_trusted_types_test.dart` (policy present, DOMPurify strips payloads); an XSS-corpus widget test rendering hostile markdown inert; a report-only vs enforce toggle test.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-002.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans, ZAP baseline)
- [ ] Threat model + controls-matrix rows updated for the web XSS control
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Enable COOP/COEP cross-origin isolation for multithreaded WASM
body:
## Context
skwasm multithreading, `SharedArrayBuffer`, and whisper.cpp threads all require **cross-origin isolation**, which needs `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` + `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: require-corp` and every cross-origin subresource sending CORP/CORS (`docs/platform/web.md` §9, ADR-0010 decision 2, secure-coding-checklist §6.2). This is why the app must live on **its own isolated origin**. Without it, `self.crossOriginIsolated` is false and the app is stuck on the slower CanvasKit main-thread path and cannot run offline whisper transcription. This issue turns on isolation, verified via a report-only rollout.

## Scope
**In:** set COOP `same-origin` and COEP `require-corp` (or `credentialless`) on the app document; ensure all first-party subresources send CORP; a `-Report-Only` staging rollout and a `self.crossOriginIsolated` runtime assertion; document the own-origin requirement.
**Out:** CSP/Trusted Types ({{SN-WEB-014}}), SRI ({{SN-WEB-016}}), the hosting config that emits these at the edge ({{SN-WEB-017}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] On Chrome/Edge with headers set, `self.crossOriginIsolated === true` and skwasm engages (paint on a Worker).
- [ ] whisper.cpp WASM threads initialise only when `crossOriginIsolated` is true; the feature is hidden otherwise (never silently degraded to cloud).
- [ ] Every first-party subresource loads under `require-corp` (no blocked resources); third-party embeds are eliminated or `credentialless`.
- [ ] A report-only phase produced zero CORP/COEP violations before enforcement.

## Technical notes
Headers set at the origin/edge ({{SN-WEB-017}}) but authored/validated here; on iOS you get CanvasKit regardless, so isolation must be optional-not-required for baseline function. Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §2/§9 and ADR-0010 decision 2. Coordinate with the whisper path ({{SN-WEB-025}}).

## Security & privacy
Cross-origin isolation also hardens against cross-window attacks (MASVS-PLATFORM-2, OWASP-A05 misconfiguration, CWE-1021). No credentials leak cross-origin; own-origin isolation reduces the embedding/clickjacking surface. No content in violation reports.

## UX notes
Invisible, but a browser lacking isolation must still open, read and light-edit notes (graceful capability degrade) — surface a subtle 'faster inking in the app' hint only where relevant (Editor chrome, `design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §7). A11y unaffected.

## Test plan
`app/integration_test/web_isolation_test.dart` (asserts `crossOriginIsolated`, skwasm/whisper gating in headless Chromium with headers); a fallback test with headers absent asserting baseline function.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-002.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Threat model row updated for the isolation control
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Add SRI and baseline security response headers to the web app
body:
## Context
Beyond CSP and isolation, the ASVS 5.0 L2 web posture requires **Subresource Integrity** on any external script/style (`integrity="sha384-…"` + `crossorigin`, enforced fleet-wide with `Integrity-Policy`) and a baseline of protective response headers: `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` (which protects the share-link URL **fragment** — TM-I-09), `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Strict-Transport-Security`, and a restrictive `Permissions-Policy` denying camera/mic/geolocation unless a feature needs them (`docs/platform/web.md` §9, secure-coding-checklist §6.2). The shipped product self-hosts assets, so SRI mainly guards the few remaining pinned externals. This task adds them all.

## Scope
**In:** SRI attributes on any external subresource + `Integrity-Policy`; `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`; `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`; `Strict-Transport-Security` with a sane max-age; a least-privilege `Permissions-Policy`.
**Out:** CSP/Trusted Types ({{SN-WEB-014}}), COOP/COEP ({{SN-WEB-015}}), the hosting/CDN that emits headers ({{SN-WEB-017}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every external subresource carries a valid `integrity` + `crossorigin`; a tampered asset is blocked by the browser (verified with a mutated hash).
- [ ] `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` is set so outbound navigations never leak the share-link fragment (TM-I-09).
- [ ] `nosniff`, `HSTS`, and a deny-by-default `Permissions-Policy` (camera/mic/geolocation off unless needed) are present.
- [ ] `securityheaders`/ZAP baseline reports no missing-header finding for these.

## Technical notes
SRI hashes generated at build and injected; headers authored here and delivered by the edge ({{SN-WEB-017}}). Prefer self-hosting over CDNs (checklist §6.2 note). Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §9 and secure-coding-checklist §6.2 SHOULD list.

## Security & privacy
MASVS-CODE-2 (supply-chain integrity), OWASP-A08, CWE-353 (missing integrity check); MASVS-PRIVACY-2 for referrer/fragment protection of share links. No secrets in headers; camera/mic denied by default (least privilege).

## UX notes
None beyond baseline (no UI). Baseline: no note content or tokens in any header or referrer; share links keep the key in the `#fragment`. A11y unaffected.

## Test plan
`app/test/web/security_headers_test.dart` (asserts each header value on the served response); a build-time SRI-generation unit test; a tampered-asset integration check.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-014, SN-WEB-015.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Controls-matrix updated for the header controls
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Provision web hosting and CDN on an isolated origin with edge headers
body:
## Context
The web app must be served over **HTTPS on its own origin** so cross-origin isolation, OPFS sync handles, clipboard, WebAuthn and the service worker all work, and so the ASVS 5.0 L2 header stack (CSP/Trusted Types/COOP/COEP/SRI + baseline headers) is delivered consistently at the edge (`docs/platform/web.md` §8/§9, ADR-0010 decision 2). This issue provisions hosting + CDN with Brotli, correct cache-control for the immutable WASM/JS chunks vs the no-cache SW, and the header stack. It needs maintainer-supplied hosting credentials/domain, so it is `needs-credentials` and not agent-ready.

## Scope
**In:** static hosting + CDN on a dedicated origin/domain; Brotli/gzip; cache-control (immutable hashed assets long-lived, `sw.js`/`index.html` no-cache); edge delivery of all security headers ({{SN-WEB-014}}/{{SN-WEB-015}}/{{SN-WEB-016}}); staged rollout with header report-only first; SBOM/provenance attach ({{SN-CI-004}}).
**Out:** authoring the header values (done in the security issues), app code, DNS/domain purchase decision (maintainer).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The app is served over HTTPS on its own origin; `self.crossOriginIsolated` holds where expected.
- [ ] All security headers are present at the edge on every response (verified by an automated post-deploy check).
- [ ] Hashed asset chunks are `cache-control: immutable`; `sw.js` and `index.html` are `no-cache`; Brotli negotiated.
- [ ] A cached PWA cold-starts < 3 s (decision 7); a staged rollout with rollback is documented.

## Technical notes
Edge config (headers, compression, cache) as code in `tools/` or the deploy workflow; pin the deploy Action to a SHA (checklist §10). Reference ADR-0010 decision 2 and `docs/security/devsecops-pipeline.md`. Requires maintainer secrets: hosting/CDN account + domain (CLAUDE.md §13 credentials).

## Security & privacy
MASVS-NETWORK-1 (TLS 1.2+, HSTS, no cleartext — CWE-319), OWASP-A05 (secure config at the edge). No secrets in the repo; credentials via CI secrets only. Access logs keep connection metadata only, with retention limits (checklist §7 SHOULD).

## UX notes
None beyond baseline; hosting is invisible. Baseline: no content or tokens in server logs or URLs. A status/health page must not leak build secrets.

## Test plan
`tools/scripts/verify_deployed_headers.mjs` (post-deploy asserts every header + TLS + HSTS); a smoke test that the deployed PWA installs and loads offline; rollback drill documented.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-014, SN-WEB-015, SN-WEB-016, SN-CI-004.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Deploy config + verification merged, CI green; post-deploy header check passing
- [ ] Runbook/ADR updated for hosting; SBOM + provenance attached
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Implement web sign-in with Google, Microsoft, Apple and passkeys
body:
## Context
Identity is optional and never required to take notes (guest mode is first-class, decision 5), but the web surface must offer the same sign-in options as native: Google (GIS), Microsoft (MSAL.js PKCE), Apple (Sign in with Apple JS redirect), plus **WebAuthn/passkeys** as the recommended passwordless primary (`docs/platform/web.md` §7). This issue wires the web implementations of the shared auth abstraction ({{SN-AUTH-003}}/{{SN-AUTH-004}}/{{SN-AUTH-005}}) using OIDC PKCE + `state` + `nonce`, storing tokens per the web reduced-guarantee posture. It needs maintainer OAuth client IDs, so it is `needs-credentials`.

## Scope
**In:** the web impls of Google/Microsoft/Apple sign-in behind the shared auth interface; WebAuthn passkey registration/assertion with conditional mediation; token handling that never persists the master key in the clear (R4).
**Out:** the shared auth abstraction and dev bypass guard (SN-AUTH-002), Drive/OneDrive authorization scopes ({{SN-WEB-019}}), profile UI (SN-ONB-001).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Each provider completes an OIDC flow with PKCE + `state` + `nonce`, all three validated; failure lands on a user-safe error, never a stack trace.
- [ ] Passkey registration + assertion works on a passkey-capable browser (conditional mediation offers it on the Login screen).
- [ ] Access tokens are short-lived with refresh rotation; nothing sensitive is written to `localStorage` in the clear (the experimental `flutter_secure_storage` web impl is not relied on for the master key — R4).
- [ ] Guest mode still reaches the full editor with no sign-in; an account takeover yields no note plaintext (keys are E2EE).

## Technical notes
`app/lib/auth/` web strategies using `google_sign_in` v7, `aad_oauth`/MSAL browser, `sign_in_with_apple` web redirect, and WebAuthn via `dart:js_interop`. Apple needs a Services ID + verified domain over HTTPS. Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §7 and secure-coding-checklist §4. Requires client IDs/secrets via CI secrets (CLAUDE.md §13).

## Security & privacy
MASVS-AUTH-1/2, OWASP-A07, CWE-287, ASVS 5.0 V6 auth. PKCE + state + nonce; tokens minimal-scope and short-lived; no secrets in code (Dart AOT reversible — checklist §9.1). Zero-knowledge preserved: identity gates sharing/entitlements only, never note access.

## UX notes
Login screen (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §3): 'Continue with Google/Microsoft/Apple' + passkey; Profiles screen follows (§4). All 17 looks + dark; buttons ≥ 44px, keyboard-reachable, visible focus, `Semantics` labels; error copy is friendly (§16). Guest 'Skip / try it now' is prominent.

## Test plan
`app/test/auth/web_signin_test.dart` (PKCE/state/nonce validation, error paths, guest bypass); a WebAuthn assertion integration test with a virtual authenticator; a token-storage assertion that no master key persists in the clear.

## Dependencies
SN-AUTH-003, SN-AUTH-004, SN-AUTH-005, SN-WEB-015.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Threat model/controls-matrix updated for web auth
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md; CODEOWNERS review of app/lib/auth

title: Implement Google Drive and OneDrive user-cloud sync on web
body:
## Context
Local-first zero-knowledge sync goes to the **user's own cloud** (decision 3): on web that means Google Drive (Drive Picker + `drive.file` scope) and OneDrive (MSAL + Microsoft Graph `Files.*`); CloudKit JS is Apple-ID-only and a long-term risk, so it is out of primary scope (`docs/platform/web.md` §7). Everything synced is **E2EE ciphertext** encrypted client-side before any write. This issue implements the web cloud-drive adapter for the shared sync engine ({{SN-SYNC-004}}/{{SN-SYNC-003}}), providing the durable copy that also protects against browser storage eviction.

## Scope
**In:** the web `sane_cloud_drive` adapter for Google Drive (`drive.file`, Picker) and OneDrive (Graph `Files.*`); upload/download of encrypted op-log segments + content-addressed blobs; chunked encryption for large attachments; a 'connect cloud' flow in Settings > Sync & backup.
**Out:** the CRDT merge/op-log engine (SN-SYNC-002), key hierarchy ({{SN-CRY-002}}), iCloud native (SN-SYNC-003 mobile).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Connecting Drive uses the `drive.file` scope only (app sees only files it creates/opens); connecting OneDrive uses least-privilege `Files.*`.
- [ ] Only ciphertext is written to the cloud; a network capture shows no plaintext note bytes (decision 3); the AEAD tag is verified before any decrypted byte is used (fail closed).
- [ ] Large attachments chunk-encrypt without loading the whole file into memory.
- [ ] Two browsers editing offline then syncing converge with no data loss (CRDT), and a synced note recovers after simulated local eviction.

## Technical notes
`plugins/sane_cloud_drive` web + `packages/sane_sync`; `googleapis` Drive, MSAL/Graph; crypto in `sane_crypto` (WebCrypto/WASM) before egress. TLS-only; no cleartext. Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §7 and `architecture/sync.md`. Requires OAuth client IDs (CLAUDE.md §13) — `needs-credentials`.

## Security & privacy
MASVS-NETWORK-1 (TLS), MASVS-CRYPTO-1 (approved AEAD, ciphertext-only egress — OWASP-A02, CWE-311). The drive is dumb transport; metadata minimised (TM-I-04). Tokens in the web secure store, short-lived; no content or file paths logged (checklist §3/§7).

## UX notes
Settings > Sync & backup (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §12): 'Connect Google Drive / OneDrive', sync status, last-synced, and the durability nudge from {{SN-WEB-009}}. All 17 looks + dark; conflict/first-run states have clear copy; keyboard-reachable; `Semantics` status announcements.

## Test plan
`packages/sane_sync/test/web_drive_adapter_test.dart` (ciphertext-only egress, tag-verify fail-closed, chunking); `app/integration_test/web_sync_convergence_test.dart` (two-client offline→sync converge); a mocked-Graph OneDrive test.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-018, SN-SYNC-004, SN-SYNC-003, SN-CRY-002.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Threat model/controls-matrix updated for web sync egress
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md; CODEOWNERS review of sane_sync

title: Implement keyboard-first navigation and shortcuts on web
body:
## Context
The web app MUST be fully **keyboard-operable** — create/search/navigate/format/undo-redo via shortcuts, visible focus rings, and skip links — because desktop web users expect it and it is a WCAG 2.2 AA requirement (decision 10, `docs/platform/web.md` §5). Because Flutter paints its UI (not native DOM), keyboard handling and focus order must be hand-built and validated. This issue delivers the web keyboard model so a user can drive the whole app without a pointer.

## Scope
**In:** a documented shortcut map (new note, search, undo/redo, tool switch, page nav, format); logical focus order + visible focus rings; skip links; `FocusTraversalGroup`/`Shortcuts`/`Actions` wiring; a discoverable shortcut cheat-sheet overlay.
**Out:** screen-reader semantics + OCR alt-text ({{SN-WEB-021}}), stylus/touch gestures ({{SN-WEB-006}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Every primary action (new note, open search, undo, redo, switch tool, next/prev page, format text) has a keyboard shortcut that works on Chrome, Safari and Firefox.
- [ ] Tab/Shift-Tab moves through a logical focus order with a visible focus ring on every interactive element; a skip-link jumps to main content.
- [ ] The full create→search→edit→undo flow is completable with no pointer.
- [ ] A '?' cheat-sheet lists shortcuts and is itself keyboard-reachable and dismissible with Esc.

## Technical notes
Flutter `Shortcuts`/`Actions`/`FocusTraversalGroup` in `app/`; ensure the canvas does not trap Tab. Avoid clashing with browser/OS shortcuts. Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §5 keyboard-first and `docs/design/accessibility.md`. Coordinate the shortcut map with the native platforms for parity.

## Security & privacy
Baseline (MASVS-PRIVACY-1): shortcut handling logs no content; a shortcut cannot trigger a network egress or cloud-AI call without the standard consent (checklist §11). No new data flow.

## UX notes
Applies across Library, Editor, Search and Settings (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html`); focus rings use the accent token per `(lookId, mode)` so they meet contrast in all 17 looks + dark. Cheat-sheet uses the overlay pattern (§8/§13). Targets ≥ 44px; respects reduced-motion.

## Test plan
`app/integration_test/web_keyboard_nav_test.dart` (drives the full flow via key events on Chrome); a widget test of focus order + skip link; a golden of the cheat-sheet in two looks.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-002.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] docs/design/accessibility.md updated if the shortcut map changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Hand-author web accessibility semantics and OCR alt-text for ink
body:
## Context
Flutter web paints text and semantics rather than emitting native DOM, so accessibility is a known weak spot (R3): the framework injects an `aria-*` semantics layer, but custom-painted content (the canvas, ink) has **no** meaning to a screen reader unless we hand-author it, and handwritten content needs **OCR-backed text alternatives** (`docs/platform/web.md` §5, ADR-0010 decision 5, decision 10). This issue provides `Semantics` for the painted surfaces and wires OCR alt-text so a screen reader can convey a handwritten note, validated on a real screen reader as an explicit gate.

## Scope
**In:** hand-authored `Semantics` for the canvas, page rail, palette dock and other painted chrome; OCR-derived text alternatives for handwritten strokes surfaced to assistive tech; enabling Flutter's semantics layer; a screen-reader validation checklist.
**Out:** the recognition engine itself ({{SN-HWR-001}}), keyboard shortcuts ({{SN-WEB-020}}), the full app a11y audit (SN-A11Y-001 / M7).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The canvas, page rail and palette dock expose meaningful `Semantics` (role + label) — no unlabeled painted controls.
- [ ] A handwritten note exposes an OCR text alternative to VoiceOver (Safari) and NVDA (Firefox/Chrome); a purely graphical stroke is labelled as such.
- [ ] Core flows (open note, switch tool, navigate pages) are operable and announced under a screen reader.
- [ ] Contrast ≥ 4.5:1 and 44px targets hold across all 17 looks + dark for interactive chrome.

## Technical notes
`app/` + `sane_ui`; wrap painted widgets in `Semantics`; feed alt-text from the recognition adapter ({{SN-HWR-001}}); note the web has no on-device ML Kit (R5) so alt-text may come from the Rust/WASM or cloud-opt-in path ({{SN-WEB-025}}). Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §5 and `docs/design/accessibility.md`. Real-screen-reader gate per ADR-0010 verify-step 6.

## Security & privacy
Baseline (MASVS-PRIVACY-1): alt-text is note content and must not be logged; if OCR uses a cloud path it requires the per-request opt-in + 'data leaves device' banner (decision 6, checklist §11). No silent egress.

## UX notes
Editor, Library, page rail, palette dock (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §6/§7). Alt-text reads naturally; a 'no text detected' fallback is graceful. All 17 looks + dark meet contrast; focus + semantics align with {{SN-WEB-020}}.

## Test plan
`app/test/web/semantics_test.dart` (asserts Semantics nodes on painted chrome); a golden/semantics-tree snapshot; a manual VoiceOver + NVDA gate recorded in {{SN-WEB-023}}.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-002, SN-A11Y-001, SN-HWR-001.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] docs/design/accessibility.md updated; screen-reader gate recorded
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Build the zero-friction 'try it now' guest flow on web
body:
## Context
'Try on web' is a core acquisition path (ADR-0010 rejects a WebView precisely because a no-install trial matters), and guest mode is first-class (decision 5). A visitor should land directly in a working editor with **no account, no permission prompts, and everything local**, then be gently nudged to install or sign in to make notes durable. This issue delivers that guest flow on web, wiring the durability guard ({{SN-WEB-009}}) and install affordance ({{SN-WEB-010}}) so a trial note is never silently lost.

## Scope
**In:** a guest entry that skips Login and opens the Editor with a starter note; local-only persistence; a non-nagging upgrade nudge (install / sign in for durability + sync); a guest→account handoff that keeps the local note.
**Out:** the account/key migration mechanics (CLAUDE.md §13 pending decision — reference only), billing/upgrade purchase (SN-BILL-001), the marketing landing page (SN-SITE-001).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Visiting the app opens a working Editor with no sign-in and no launch-time permission prompts (permissions requested lazily, in-context — checklist §8).
- [ ] A guest note persists locally across reload and shows the eviction-risk nudge from {{SN-WEB-009}}.
- [ ] An upgrade nudge (install / sign in) is present but dismissible and remembered (per-viewer localStorage); it never blocks note-taking.
- [ ] Signing in from guest preserves the in-progress local note (no data loss at handoff).

## Technical notes
`app/` onboarding/router (go_router) guest route; reuse the guest auth state from SN-AUTH-002; telemetry stays off (opt-in) and no analytics SDK is linked (checklist §8/§10). Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §7 (guest first-class) and `docs/design/screens-and-flows.md` §3/§5.

## Security & privacy
MASVS-PRIVACY-1/2 + MASVS-STORAGE-1: no identifiers created for a guest; no background egress; local data encrypted at rest where crypto is present; the privacy dashboard reflects guest reality (checklist §11). No content in logs.

## UX notes
Entry from Login 'Skip / try it now' and the marketing CTA (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §3, Onboarding §5). Starter note demonstrates pen + text. All 17 looks + dark; nudge is a calm banner (§16 microcopy), ≥ 44px, keyboard-reachable, `Semantics` labelled.

## Test plan
`app/integration_test/web_guest_flow_test.dart` (guest entry, local persist across reload, sign-in handoff preserves the note, no launch-time prompt); a golden of the upgrade nudge in two looks.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-009, SN-WEB-010.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Code + tests merged, CI green (lint, analyze, unit, security scans)
- [ ] Docs updated if the guest flow changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Build the cross-browser test harness and support-matrix runs
body:
## Context
Web support is tiered (`docs/platform/compatibility-matrix.md` §3, `docs/platform/web.md` §12): **Tier 1 (CI)** is Chrome desktop (the ≤ 30 ms ink gate + functional/golden/PWA/offline runs); **Tier 2 manual** is Safari iPadOS/macOS, Firefox, Edge, Samsung Internet; plus a screen-reader gate (VoiceOver + NVDA) and a storage-eviction test. This issue builds the harness that runs the Tier 1 suite automatically and defines/records the Tier 2 manual matrix each release, so a browser regression is caught rather than shipped.

## Scope
**In:** a headless-Chromium `integration_test` runner in CI for functional + PWA/offline/service-worker + renderer-fallback checks; a documented Tier 2 manual checklist template; the screen-reader gate procedure; a storage-eviction/ITP simulation test.
**Out:** the Lighthouse/perf-budget gate ({{SN-WEB-024}}), individual feature tests (each ships its own).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] CI runs the web integration suite on headless Chromium on every PR and blocks on failure (Tier 1).
- [ ] A Tier 2 manual checklist (Safari iPadOS/macOS, Firefox, Edge, Samsung Internet) exists and is filled each release with known-gap notes.
- [ ] The screen-reader gate (VoiceOver via Safari, NVDA via Firefox/Chrome) over core flows is documented and recorded.
- [ ] A storage-eviction/7-day-ITP simulation confirms a synced note recovers (ties {{SN-WEB-009}}).

## Technical notes
`app/integration_test/` + a CI web job (Chrome for Testing/`chromedriver`); Playwright/`patrol` where native-browser automation is needed (`docs/platform/web.md` §12). Reference the compatibility matrix §2 (Web-Chrome-desktop reference slot) and §3. Pin CI Actions to SHAs (checklist §10).

## Security & privacy
Baseline (MASVS-CODE-1): the harness uses no production secrets; test fixtures contain no real tokens/PII (checklist §0/§7). Eviction test uses synthetic notes only.

## UX notes
None beyond baseline (test infrastructure). The manual checklist references the design screens (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html`) so a tester exercises Login/Library/Editor/Search/Settings in each browser across looks.

## Test plan
`tools/device_lab/web_matrix.md` (manual template); `app/integration_test/web_smoke_test.dart` (Tier 1 functional/PWA); `app/integration_test/web_eviction_test.dart`; screen-reader gate runbook.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-002, SN-FND-003.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Harness + checklist merged, CI green; Tier 1 web job blocking
- [ ] Compatibility-matrix doc updated if tiers changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Add Lighthouse PWA and web perf/ink budgets to CI
body:
## Context
The web release has hard gates (`docs/platform/web.md` §8, ADR-0010 verify-steps 2-3, decision 7): a **Lighthouse PWA** pass (installable, offline, valid manifest + SW), a **< 3 s cached cold start**, and the **≤ 30 ms pen-to-pixel** Tier B ink budget on Chrome desktop. This issue wires those into CI so a regression blocks merge, using the shared latency harness ({{SN-PERF-002}}) in web mode and Lighthouse CI, recorded per release like the native perf gates.

## Scope
**In:** Lighthouse CI (PWA + performance categories) with thresholds; a web-mode run of the latency harness asserting ≤ 30 ms on the Chrome-desktop reference; a cached-cold-start assertion (< 3 s); trend recording per release.
**Out:** the bundle-size budget ({{SN-WEB-003}}), the functional/matrix harness ({{SN-WEB-023}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Lighthouse CI runs on every PR touching web and fails if PWA-installable/offline or the performance threshold regresses.
- [ ] `tools/perf_harness` (web mode) asserts ≤ 30 ms pen-to-pixel on the Web-Chrome-desktop reference; a regression fails CI (decision 7).
- [ ] A cached PWA cold start is measured < 3 s and recorded; the number is attached to the run.
- [ ] Results are stored as a per-release trend artifact.

## Technical notes
Lighthouse CI in the web workflow; extend `tools/perf_harness` ({{SN-PERF-002}}) with a web driver measuring input-to-paint via the browser timeline. Reference `docs/platform/performance-budgets.md`, `docs/platform/web.md` §8/§12, and ADR-0010 verify-steps. Pin Actions to SHAs (checklist §10).

## Security & privacy
Baseline (MASVS-CODE-1): the perf job uses no production secrets and no real user data; measurement logs contain no note content (checklist §7). Lighthouse runs against a disposable staging build.

## UX notes
None beyond baseline (CI gate). Indirectly protects the Editor/Library UX by keeping cold start and ink latency within budget across all 17 looks (perf is look-agnostic).

## Test plan
`tools/perf_harness/test/web_latency_harness_test.dart` (harness self-check on a fixture trace); a CI dry-run asserting Lighthouse thresholds trigger on a seeded regression; the cold-start assertion.

## Dependencies
SN-WEB-023, SN-PERF-002.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Gate + tests merged, CI green; web perf/Lighthouse job blocking
- [ ] performance-budgets.md updated if web thresholds changed
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md

title: Decide and implement the web handwriting-recognition path
body:
## Context
Google **ML Kit is mobile-only — there is no web build**, so the web surface has **no on-device digital-ink recognition** out of the box (R5, `docs/platform/web.md` §6). ADR-0010 decision 6 requires the web path to be either a **Rust/WASM (or whisper-style WASM) recognition core** gated behind cross-origin isolation, or a **cloud OCR/ink path as an explicit per-request opt-in** with the 'data leaves device' indicator (decision 6) — never a silent cloud send. The choice must be recorded in ADR-0010; this issue carries the `needs-decision` and implements the chosen path once the maintainer decides. It also feeds OCR alt-text ({{SN-WEB-021}}).

## Scope
**In:** implement the maintainer-chosen path — Rust/WASM recognition core via `flutter_rust_bridge` (offline, behind COOP/COEP) OR a cloud opt-in path with the mandatory banner; a capability check that hides recognition on web when neither is available; record the decision in ADR-0010.
**Out:** the recognition engine on mobile ({{SN-HWR-001}}), transcription/audio ({{SN-WEB} audio}), the isolation headers ({{SN-WEB-015}}).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The chosen path is recorded in ADR-0010 and reflected in `docs/platform/web.md` §6.
- [ ] If Rust/WASM: recognition runs fully offline where `crossOriginIsolated` is true; if unavailable, recognition is hidden (never silently cloud).
- [ ] If cloud opt-in: no ink/text leaves the browser without a per-request opt-in and a visible 'data leaves device' banner (decision 6, checklist §11).
- [ ] Recognition output feeds search and OCR alt-text ({{SN-WEB-021}}) with a confidence + correction affordance.

## Technical notes
`packages/sane_ml` interfaces + a web adapter (`flutter_rust_bridge` WASM or a gated cloud client); isolation prerequisite from {{SN-WEB-015}}. Reference `docs/platform/web.md` §6 recognition gap, ADR-0010 decision 6, ADR-0016 (on-device ML/AI). Maintainer decision pending (CLAUDE.md §13: MyScript vs ML-Kit-only relates on native; web path is the WASM-vs-cloud choice).

## Security & privacy
MASVS-PRIVACY-1/3 + OWASP-A08: no silent egress; cloud path is explicit opt-in with the banner and no-training/ephemeral guarantees; ink/text are content and not logged. A WASM core keeps data on-device.

## UX notes
Recognition surfaces in Search (`design/Sane Notes.dc.html` §11) and convert-to-text in the Editor; the 'data leaves device' banner is unmissable when a cloud path is used. All 17 looks + dark; correction UI keyboard-reachable, `Semantics` labelled.

## Test plan
`packages/sane_ml/test/web_recognition_test.dart` (chosen-path adapter, offline gating or opt-in gating); an abuse test asserting no egress without opt-in; a search-integration test on recognised text.

## Dependencies
SN-HWR-001, SN-WEB-015.

## Definition of done
- [ ] Decision recorded in ADR-0010; code + tests merged, CI green
- [ ] Threat model/controls-matrix updated if a cloud egress was added
- [ ] Reviewed against docs/security/secure-coding-checklist.md
